Vendored fork of upstream navigation_rail_m3e 0.3.5. The patched sources live in this repo at packages/navigation_rail_m3e/lib/src/. The patch is activated by the root pubspec.yaml dependency_overrides path: entry — remove that entry and flutter pub get silently reverts to upstream.

Overview & role

navigation_rail_m3e is a leaf Material 3 Expressive UI widget package. Hexagonal / domain-layer concerns are N/A — it has no data, service, or routing surface. It renders a responsive navigation rail and consumes m3e_design tokens plus three sibling M3E packages (fab_m3e, icon_button_m3e, button_m3e).

This package is one of four vendored forks of EmilyMoonstone/material_3_expressive pinned in this repo (alongside fab_m3e, split_button_m3e, toolbar_m3e). It is the only fork with multiple patched files and the only fork with no test/ — the highest test debt of the four.

What this is

A vendored fork of upstream navigation_rail_m3e 0.3.5. The fork is pulled in transitively via the m3e_collection umbrella package, and activated by a path: dependency_overrides entry in the root pubspec.yaml. The root override comment names all four patched files (navigation_rail_m3e_widget.dart, rail_item_button_m3e.dart, rail_tokens_adapter.dart, rail_theme.dart). Patch markers in source use the // Fork patch: form.

Glossary

  • Fork — a vendored copy of an upstream package, edited in-tree, pinned by a path: override.
  • Override — the dependency_overrides: block in the root pubspec.yaml that forces pub to resolve this package from a local folder instead of pub.dev.
  • Patch marker — an inline comment tag (// Patched (vendored fork), // Fork patch:, or // PATCH) that flags every block of code changed from upstream. Audit with grep -rEni 'fork|patch|vendored' packages/navigation_rail_m3e/lib (case-insensitive — this fork's markers use Fork patch: with a capital F).
  • Re-sync — the procedure for re-applying this fork's patches onto a newer upstream version (see §9).
  • M3E — Material 3 Expressive, the motion/shape system this widget implements.

Architecture — the fork contract

The fork contract (shared)

Every vendored fork in this repo carries the same contract:

  • The WHY is documented in the root pubspec.yaml dependency_overrides comment block above each path: entry. Read it before editing.
  • The HOW is flagged in source with // Patched (vendored fork), // Fork patch:, or // PATCH. Every changed block has a marker.
  • The audit command is grep -rEni 'fork|patch|vendored' packages/<name>/lib (case-insensitive). Re-run after every edit and before every re-sync.
  • The doc-gap checklist (every fork carries this debt): add a > Vendored fork of upstream <name> <version> banner to the README; backfill the CHANGELOG; fix the EmilyMonestone → EmilyMoonstone typo in issue_tracker (present in every fork's pubspec.yaml).
  • The test contract: every fork SHOULD ship a test/. navigation_rail_m3e currently has NONE (highest debt); the other three forks do ship one.

Public API reference

The barrel lib/navigation_rail_m3e.dart exports 10 symbols. The fork only changes internals; the public signatures are unchanged from upstream.

NavigationRailM3E

packages/navigation_rail_m3e/lib/src/navigation_rail_m3e_widget.dart

class NavigationRailM3E extends StatefulWidget {
  const NavigationRailM3E({
    this.type = NavigationRailM3EType.expanded,
    this.modality = NavigationRailM3EModality.standard,
    required this.sections,
    required this.selectedIndex,
    required this.onDestinationSelected,
    this.fab,
    this.hideWhenCollapsed = false,
    this.expandedWidth,
    this.onDismissModal,
    this.onTypeChanged,
    this.labelBehavior = NavigationRailM3ELabelBehavior.alwaysShow,
    this.scrollable = true,
    this.trailing,
    this.trailingAtBottom = true,
    this.background,
  });
}
  • type L3: NavigationRailM3EType: expanded / collapsed / alwaysCollapsed / alwaysExpanded. The fork's didUpdateWidget honors host type changes (the upstream silently ignored them after first build).
  • modality L4: standard (in-flow) or modal (overlay + scrim).
  • sections L5: List; each section has destinations and an optional header.
  • fab L8: Optional NavigationRailM3EFabSlot — wraps a FabM3E or ExtendedFabM3E for the top cluster.
  • hideWhenCollapsed L10: When true + type collapsed, rail animates to width 0 (collapsed-peek overlay still drawn).
  • expandedWidth L11: Clamped to theme bounds (220-360).

Models + enums

Models: NavigationRailM3ESection (= RailSectionM3E), NavigationRailM3EDestination (= RailDestinationM3E), NavigationRailM3EFabSlot (= RailFabSlot), RailMenuSlot. Enums: NavigationRailM3EType (type.dart), NavigationRailM3EModality (modality.dart), NavigationRailM3ELabelBehavior. All unchanged from upstream — the fork only edits how the widget renders and animates, not what the host configures.

class NavigationRailTokensAdapter {
  const NavigationRailTokensAdapter(this.context);
  ShapeBorder get indicatorShapeFull => const StadiumBorder();
  // containerColor, activeIndicatorColor, activeIconAndLabel, badge*, ...
}
  • Fork patch L6: itemExpandedHeight = 56 (was 40 upstream). Reduces the swap jump between collapsed (66) and expanded layouts.
  • NavigationRailTokensAdapter L14: Bridges m3e_design tokens with Theme.of(context) fallbacks.
  • Fork patch L16: indicatorShapeFull returns StadiumBorder() — corner.full per m3.material.io token table, not round.xs.

RailItemButtonM3E

RailItemButtonM3E is the internal per-destination button (exported for advanced hosts). It renders expanded (Row: icon + label + badge, wrapped in a Material with indicatorShapeFull when selected) or collapsed (Column: IconButtonM3E + label). Fork patch: only the expanded indicator uses the corner.full Material — the collapsed pill is drawn by IconButtonM3E's round shape variant; mixing the two would clip corner glyphs.

Usage playbook

example/rail_usage.dart

import 'package:m3e_collection/m3e_collection.dart';

NavigationRailM3E(
  type: NavigationRailM3EType.expanded,
  modality: NavigationRailM3EModality.standard,
  selectedIndex: 0,
  onDestinationSelected: (i) {},
  sections: [
    NavigationRailM3ESection(destinations: [
      NavigationRailM3EDestination(icon: const Icon(Icons.inbox), label: const Text('Inbox')),
      NavigationRailM3EDestination(icon: const Icon(Icons.settings), label: const Text('Settings')),
    ]),
  ],
)
  • type + modality L4-5: Toggle via onTypeChanged to let the built-in menu button drive collapse; or set type directly — the fork's didUpdateWidget honors either path.

5b. Wiring — how a host actually gets this fork

pubspec.yaml (root)

# Vendored fork of navigation_rail_m3e 0.3.5 (pulled in via m3e_collection).
# Patched so the expand/collapse transition lays content out at the target
# width behind a ClipRect+OverflowBox reveal (no transient RenderFlex
# overflow, no label squish), uses the M3E spatial-spring fallback curve,
# fades labels in, honors type changes from the host, and fixes indicator/
# container corners to spec (corner.full pill indicators, corner.large modal
# container). Patches: packages/navigation_rail_m3e/lib/src/
# navigation_rail_m3e_widget.dart, rail_item_button_m3e.dart,
# rail_tokens_adapter.dart.
dependency_overrides:
  navigation_rail_m3e:
    path: packages/navigation_rail_m3e
  • WHY L1-8: Root pubspec.yaml override comment — the auditable reason for the fork. Edit whenever the patch list changes.
  • HOW L9-11: path: override activates the fork. m3e_collection still re-exports navigation_rail_m3e by name; the override redirects that name to the local folder.

Hosts almost never import package:navigation_rail_m3e/... directly. The fork is pulled in transitively via m3e_collection (the umbrella that re-exports every M3E widget), and most apps reach it through appbox_kit's Kit* wrappers. The root dependency_overrides path: entry is the only thing that activates the patch — m3e_collection's own version constraint is unchanged. The fork also has cross-deps on three sibling M3E forks/packages: fab_m3e ^0.1.1, icon_button_m3e ^0.2.1, button_m3e ^0.1.1 (which is why pubspec.lock is committed here).

Features appendix

  • Collapsed rail (icon-only, 96dp)Standard mode + optional collapsed-peek overlay when hideWhenCollapsed.
  • Expanded rail (220-360dp, labels)Configurable via expandedWidth, clamped to theme bounds.
  • Single-controller width + cross-fade transition (fork)_widthT drives both width and layer opacities; reverse uses _expandCurve.flipped so collapse starts moving immediately.
  • ClipRect + OverflowBox reveal (fork)Both layouts always mounted at target width; no transient RenderFlex overflow, no label squish.
  • Standard + modal modality
  • Modal scrim + onDismissModal
  • Sections with headers + per-section destinations
  • RailBadgeM3E numeric badges
  • Built-in FAB slot (wraps FabM3E / ExtendedFabM3E)
  • corner.full pill indicators + corner.large modal container (fork)indicatorShapeFull = StadiumBorder(); rail_tokens_adapter + rail_item_button fix.
  • Honors host type changes after first build (fork)didUpdateWidget's last else-if branch; upstream silently ignored these.

Gotchas + re-sync procedure

The fork uses FadeTransition (repaint only) for layer cross-fades — never Opacity. Opacity during animation triggers saveLayer per frame, a documented perf anti-pattern. Do not "simplify" back to Opacity.

The reverse curve is _expandCurve.flipped, NOT _expandCurve. A straight time-reversal would spend its first ~300ms inside the spring's overshoot tail (width frozen at ~220) and read as lag. If you change _expandCurve, re-test both directions.

This is the only one of the four forks with no test/. Re-syncs and edits are uninsured — every change must be smoke-tested manually in the consuming showcase (appbox_kit_showcase). Adding a test/navigation_rail_m3e_test.dart that asserts the Stack-of-two-layouts structure and the corner.full indicator is the single highest-value investment.

This fork depends on three other M3E packages (fab_m3e, icon_button_m3e, button_m3e). When re-syncing upstream, all four cross-deps must remain compatible — pubspec.lock is committed here precisely so a transitive resolution drift cannot silently break the rail. Re-run flutter pub get after any cross-dep bump and commit the new lock.

Re-sync procedure (shared across all four forks)

When bumping upstream (fab_m3e, navigation_rail_m3e, split_button_m3e, or toolbar_m3e):

1. Bump the fork's pubspec.yaml version: and the root pubspec.yaml override comment's stated version. 2. Backfill the fork's CHANGELOG.md with the new version entry (every fork's CHANGELOG is stale — see §11). 3. Diff each patched file against the new upstream release of the same path. For this fork, that is four files: navigation_rail_m3e_widget.dart, rail_item_button_m3e.dart, rail_tokens_adapter.dart, rail_theme.dart. 4. Re-apply each // Patched (vendored fork) / // Fork patch: / // PATCH block by hand. Do NOT copy upstream over the fork blindly — the markers are your only map of what to preserve. 5. Update the root pubspec.yaml override comment if the WHY or the patched-file list changed. 6. Run the fork's flutter test in packages/<name>/ (this fork has none — extra reason to add one), then run the consuming showcase (appbox_kit_showcase) to confirm the patched behaviour still renders.

Override hygiene (shared)

Never remove a dependency_overrides path: entry without first confirming upstream includes the fix. A "clean" flutter pub get silently reverts the fork to the pub.dev release, and the patch — including its bug fix — disappears with no compile error. The root override comment is the only durable record of why the patch exists.

Doc-gap debt every fork carries: (a) no > Vendored fork of upstream <name> <version> banner in the README; (b) stale CHANGELOG.md; (c) EmilyMonestone → EmilyMoonstone typo in issue_tracker (present in every fork's pubspec.yaml).

Decisions / ADRs

None. The fork contract is documented in the root pubspec.yaml override comment; no separate ADR was written. Given this fork patches four files (the most of the four), it is the strongest candidate for a dedicated ADR if the patch surface grows further.
